newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran questions foreign oil deals in Caspian-paper.
newsitem.headline: Iran questions foreign oil deals in Caspian-paper.

text.p: Iran has criticised oil deals between Caspian Sea states and foreign companies which are not approved by other countries bordering the waters, an Iranian newspaper said on Wednesday.

The criticism came days after Azerbaijan signed deals said to be worth $8 billion with four major U.S. oil firms to explore and develop oil and gas properties in the Azerbaijani sector of the Caspian Sea.
Iranian Vice-President Mahmoud Vaezi was quoted by the daily Salam as saying irregular deals, "will certainly cause problems."
Contracts, "signed without considering the rights of other states with interests in this sea lack legal basis and guarantees," Vaezi was reported as adding.
"Iran does not deny the rights and interests of Caspian Sea states to exploit the sea's resources in a logical and lawful manner," he went on.
"But some countries have caused unrest in this sensitive region through unilateral contracts with foreign companies," he added, without naming Azerbaijan.
Azerbaijan's state oil company SOCAR on Friday signed production-sharing agreements with Exxon Corp, Mobil Corp, Chevron Corp, while Amoco Corp signed a development deal.
The five states bordering the Caspian Sea -- Azerbaijan, Russia, Iran, Turkmenistan and Kazakhstan -- are in dispute over whether it is a sea or a lake, which affects its development.
Russia and Iran say it is a lake and so should be developed jointly by all sides. But Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan and Turkmenistan say that it is a sea and should be split into separate territories.
